actions.title: Prepare one preserved recovery attempt
actions.instruction: At the root of your Academy clone on a clean main branch, run Prepare in a native terminal. Academy creates the numbered attempt and freezes the stale context, provenance record, and unrelated note before you inspect anything.
actions.rationale: A prepared commit gives Check a fixed before-state and keeps a failed recovery attempt inspectable.
actions.expected_result: Academy prints academy/P06-context-drift-recovery/ATTEMPT_NUMBER and leaves you on that numbered branch.
actions.recovery: If Prepare names a dirty worktree or branch condition, preserve the message and resolve only that condition. Do not reset, rebase, or delete an earlier attempt.
actions.evidence: The prepared commit is the trusted baseline for every later byte and history comparison.

actions.title: Have the agent expose the contradictory evidence
actions.instruction: In your selected CodeArbiter harness, ask the agent to read the prepared context, provenance, preserved note, current CLI source, and ADR-0005 without editing. The agent must show why the context is stale before you select a recovery route.
actions.rationale: The correction is justified by a tracked source contradiction, not by guessing that documentation is old.

actions.expected_result: You can see that stable text is the default, structured JSON is optional, ADR-0005 replaced the lifecycle reference, and docs/preserved-note.md is outside the repair.
actions.recovery: If any named evidence file is missing or differs from the prepared scenario, stop and preserve the attempt. Use Reset for a fresh prepared baseline; do not substitute evidence.
actions.evidence: This inspection supports your decision, but Check later verifies committed objects rather than an agent transcript.

actions.title: Run the host context audit
actions.instruction: Run this CodeArbiter command in the selected harness. It is a CodeArbiter command, not a shell command, so it never begins with !. Read the finding before choosing the route.
actions.rationale: The host audit makes the available context-recovery routes visible before the scope is changed.
actions.expected_result: The agent identifies the contradicted context claim and offers a scoped recovery decision instead of silently rewriting broad repository context.
actions.recovery: If the host reports an unrelated blocker, preserve its finding and resolve that blocker first. Do not claim the audit ran by writing a replacement receipt.
actions.evidence: The final handoff records your declared route; Check does not prove that the host command ran.

actions.title: Select the bounded re-scout decision
actions.instruction: Choose scoped re-scout because the prepared source contradicts the recorded claim and ADR-0005 superseded the older lifecycle reference. Do not choose an alternate route or a broader documentation rewrite.
actions.rationale: Re-scout refreshes one source-backed claim while preserving unrelated evidence and the prepared exercise boundary.
actions.expected_result: The next instruction is limited to the stale report statement, its lifecycle link, and the provenance entry that names the source.
actions.recovery: If you cannot explain the contradiction from the prepared files, return to the evidence inspection instead of making a route choice.
actions.evidence: The handoff later declares re-scout, but that declaration is not proof of a host invocation or of your reasoning process.

actions.title: Ask the agent for the exact two-file correction
actions.instruction: Send the bounded correction instruction in the selected harness. The agent edits and stages only the two correction files, then stops for your review; it does not commit the handoff yet.
actions.rationale: Separating the correction from the handoff makes the two-commit topology reconstructable.

actions.expected_result: The staged path list contains exactly .codearbiter/CONTEXT.md and .codearbiter/.provenance/CONTEXT.json.
actions.recovery: If any other path is staged or the note changed, stop. Preserve the attempt and use Reset rather than unstaging around an unclear correction.
actions.evidence: The first learner commit is allowed to contain only the corrected context and provenance objects.

actions.title: Review the first commit boundary yourself
actions.instruction: Ask the active harness to show the staged path list and staged diff. Confirm that only the exact stale statement, lifecycle reference, and one provenance hash changed. Do not commit until the boundary is exact.
actions.rationale: A small staged review prevents a correct concept from becoming an oversized recovery commit.
actions.expected_result: You can account for both staged paths and see no change to docs/preserved-note.md.
actions.recovery: If the review shows an unrelated change, keep the attempt as evidence and use Reset for a new numbered baseline. Do not amend or rebase committed work.
actions.evidence: Check reconstructs the committed path boundary; it does not authenticate that you personally viewed this review.

actions.title: Commit the correction through CodeArbiter
actions.instruction: After your staged-boundary review, run the CodeArbiter commit gate in the selected harness. This command never begins with !.
actions.rationale: The correction must become the first of exactly two linear commits after Prepare.
actions.expected_result: The first descendant of Prepare contains exactly the two correction paths and leaves the worktree clean.
actions.recovery: If the commit gate blocks, preserve its finding and resolve the named issue without expanding the two-file correction scope.
actions.evidence: Check reads commit ancestry and changed paths, not a commit message chosen by a learner.

actions.title: Generate the digest-bound recovery handoff
actions.instruction: In a native terminal at the Academy clone root, run the local Academy helper. It derives a candidate only from committed Git objects and leaves it untracked and unstaged for your review.
actions.rationale: The lesson teaches evidence-led recovery, not hand-authoring canonical JSON or blob hashes.
actions.expected_result: Only .codearbiter/reports/academy/P06-recovery.json is untracked. It names re-scout and has identical preserved-note digests; it is not staged or committed.
actions.recovery: If the helper refuses, preserve its message and use Reset for a fresh attempt. Do not create, overwrite, stage, or hand-edit a substitute handoff.
actions.evidence: The helper derives a candidate from committed objects. Check later recomputes it and does not prove that a host command ran.

actions.title: Stage only the generated handoff
actions.instruction: In the native terminal at the Academy clone root, stage only the generated handoff. Do not stage the preserved note, correction files, or any substitute report.
actions.rationale: The learner-visible staging boundary keeps the generated evidence separate from the earlier correction and makes the second commit reviewable.
actions.expected_result: The staged path list contains only .codearbiter/reports/academy/P06-recovery.json, ready for the second-commit review.
actions.recovery: If the staged path list contains any other entry, stop and use Reset for a fresh attempt. Do not unstage around an unclear boundary or stage a replacement report.
actions.evidence: Only this staged handoff path may become the second commit; the next action reviews that exact boundary.

actions.title: Review the handoff as the second commit
actions.instruction: Ask the active harness to show the staged handoff and path list. Confirm that it is the only staged file, names re-scout, identifies the prepared and correction commits, and preserves identical note digests.
actions.rationale: The handoff is evidence about the repair, so its own commit must stay separate from the correction it describes.
actions.expected_result: The staged boundary contains one canonical report and no recreated or edited preserved note.
actions.recovery: If the handoff mixes another path or claims a different route, stop and use Reset. Do not amend the first correction commit.
actions.evidence: Check verifies the report shape, digests, and commit order; it cannot prove who generated the JSON.

actions.title: Commit the handoff through CodeArbiter
actions.instruction: After your handoff review, run the CodeArbiter commit gate in the selected harness. This is the second and final learner commit for P06.
actions.rationale: A dedicated evidence commit preserves the ordered distinction between correction and recovery record.
actions.expected_result: There are exactly two ordered single-parent commits after Prepare, and git status --short prints nothing.
actions.recovery: If the commit gate blocks, preserve its finding and correct only the named report condition in a new numbered attempt; do not amend history.
actions.evidence: The verifier requires the second commit to introduce only the handoff.

actions.title: Run the external Academy Check
actions.instruction: From the Academy clone root, run Check in a native terminal after the second commit leaves the worktree clean.
actions.rationale: The installed verifier evaluates the attempt from outside the learner flow and recomputes the evidence from Git objects.
actions.expected_result: Check prints checkpoint P06-context-drift-recovery: passed; progress: .academy/progress.json.
actions.recovery: If Check fails, preserve the committed attempt and read the failed predicate. Use Reset for a fresh numbered attempt instead of rewriting committed evidence.
actions.evidence: A pass verifies the frozen baseline, exact two-commit topology, object bytes, provenance repair, handoff, and clean worktree.

actions.title: Return to main after a passing Check
actions.instruction: After Check passes, return to main in a native terminal. Leave the completed numbered attempt branch intact for later inspection.
actions.rationale: A completed attempt remains evidence. Returning to main prepares the clone for the next published lesson without erasing the recovery history.
actions.expected_result: You are back on main and the completed academy/P06-context-drift-recovery/ATTEMPT_NUMBER branch still exists.
actions.recovery: If Check did not pass, stay on the preserved attempt and use Reset instead. Do not delete, force-reset, or rebase the completed or failed branch.
actions.evidence: The retained attempt branch remains the inspectable recovery record; returning to main is not part of Check.

actions.title: Create a preserved numbered retry
actions.instruction: Use Reset only when the attempt needs a new baseline. Run it in a native terminal at the Academy clone root; it archives the earlier branch before preparing the next number.
actions.rationale: A retained failed attempt is evidence you can inspect, not debris to erase.
actions.expected_result: Academy archives the earlier attempt and prints the next academy/P06-context-drift-recovery/ATTEMPT_NUMBER branch.
actions.recovery: If Reset stops, preserve its message and current branch. Resolve only the named repository condition; never force-reset, rebase, or delete the prior attempt.
actions.evidence: The archived branch remains reachable while the new attempt starts from the canonical prepared scenario.
